properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-24, in his words: "that reflow2 becomes that 'web of rules' for an IFC plans?"

CONTEXT. The agent had just explained why an IFC brought into Revit is a "dumb" model. Revit's model is a set of rules: a wall's top is tied to Level 2, a door is hosted in its wall, a room is bounded by its walls, and schedules and sheets are generated from the model. Raise a level and all of it follows. IFC records the result, not the rules (like a STEP export without the feature tree). Seth's Wetmore export is the Reference View: 3,626 triangle meshes, no extrusions, no materials. The question: could reflow2 hold that web instead, so a change made in an IFC copy knows what it drags with it? Seth's own example is the trigger: remove the basement storage and the two east units, which "triggers a bunch of design 'redos'... engineering calcs, soil removal".

🛑 SETTLED GROUND THIS MUST NOT QUIETLY REOPEN. reflow2:dec:idea-physical-domains-need-ordered-parts-dimensioned-quantities-and-a-physical-medium (deferred on @ajs's word, 2026-10-13) set the dividing line. The design holds what a part must MEET: requirements, limits, and the interface dimensions other parts depend on. The CAD, IFC and calculator files hold its GEOMETRY and COMPUTED values, which the design points to by file and checksum. That decision also says nothing is built "until the next physical design asks again". This is that ask, from SeattleArch.

THE WEB HAS TWO LAYERS, and the line falls between them:
· GEOMETRIC ASSOCIATIVITY: this wall's top is at that level, this door cuts that wall, this room's boundary is those walls. That is geometry, so by the 10-13 line it lives in the model file.
· CONSEQUENCES: what a part must meet, what depends on what, and which calcs, trades and sheets a change reaches. That is design intent, so it is what reflow2 already holds.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
(a) THE BUILDING'S LIMITS AS RULES. Heights, unit areas, unit count, egress, setbacks and parking ratio, each a Constraint with its unit and source, checked against the model after every edit. Inside the line; it EXISTS today. SeattleArch already found the roof 3 7/16" over its height limit and all 24 unit areas off the area table. ⚠️ The gap is measured: reflow2:fact:seattlearch-defect-findings-on-its-limits-reach-no-loop-or-gap-report-2026-10-23 (those findings reach no report). CHEAPEST.
(b) A WEB OF CONSEQUENCES, NOT GEOMETRY. The building's parts at the grain a redo happens (units, the basement, foundation, structure, excavation, egress, MEP risers, each sheet), joined by what depends on what. propagate_change on "remove the two east basement units" then returns the redo list by trade: the structural calcs, the foundation walls, the soil removal, the unit count and so on. This is reflow2's core move, impact analysis, pointed at a building. Inside the line. ⚠️ Cost: someone has to model the parts and dependencies, with the agent drafting from the IFC and the 162-page plan set and the architect or Seth checking it. That is real work per building, and it is only as right as the dependencies drawn. MEDIUM.
(c) RECOMPUTABLE NUMBERS. Excavation volume = removed footprint × depth, the unit count, the rentable area: each a recorded flo2-calc computation the design points to, so a changed input names every number that must be re-run. Inside the line (computed values stay in the calculator's files). It pairs with (b). SMALL to MEDIUM: flo2-calc exists.
(d) GEOMETRIC ASSOCIATIVITY IN reflow2, the Revit-like layer. reflow2 stores "wall W top = Level 2" and "door D hosted in W", and an edit to the IFC copy is re-solved from them. 🛑 THIS WOULD REOPEN THE 10-13 DIVIDING LINE, and is recorded only as that reopening, @ajs's call. ⚠️ Counter-arguments: it is rebuilding the core of Revit, the LARGEST option by far. Seth's file has no parameters to drive (triangles, not extrusions), so every element would first be rebuilt as a real shape. And it makes two webs that can disagree: Revit's, which the architect keeps, and ours.
(d') THE SAME LAYER, KEPT IN THE FILE. IFC itself carries some of the web: IfcRelVoidsElement/IfcRelFillsElement (door to opening to wall), IfcRelSpaceBoundary (room to walls), containment by storey. flo2-ifc could read those relations and keep them true when editing, so moving a wall moves its doors and re-bounds its rooms. This is IfcOpenShell editing work in flo2-ifc, NOT reflow2, and inside the line. (Recalled, not checked: Bonsai, IfcOpenShell's Blender front end, regenerates openings this way.) MEDIUM to LARGE; much better on a Design Transfer View export than on triangles.
(e) THE CODE AS RULES. The building code and land-use code as rules checked against the model. ⚠️ Counter: interpreting code is the architect's accountable judgement (reflow2:req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off). At most this flags what a reviewer must look at, never passes it. LARGE, with liability.

═══ A RANKING, WHICH IS A FINDING AND NOT A DECISION ═══
(a) first: it exists, and its one gap is measured. (b) and (c) together are the real "web" for Seth's question, the part that answers "what does this change drag with it". Both are inside the settled line, and it is what reflow2 is for. (d') is the right home for the geometric layer if we want it, because it lives in the file. (d) is the largest and reopens settled ground. (e) is flags only.

THE HONEST LIMIT. reflow2 will not know what a footing is. It can hold what depends on what, with units and sources, and say what a change reaches. The domain's tools (flo2-ifc, flo2-calc, and the engineers) know the rest.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-24: a building's "web of rules" is split along the 10-13 line. reflow2 holds the limits, the web of consequences and recomputable numbers, options (a), (b) and (c). The geometric links stay in the IFC file, kept true by the fork's editing, option (d'). Revit-style geometry in reflow2 (d) and code checking (e) were not taken.
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill: one open question, its options in the decision text, nothing promoted. Recorded in reflow2's design because reflow2 is what would become the web. It touches flo2 (the what-if idea for Seth) and flo2-ifc (option d'), each linked rather than copied. Accepted intent was searched first: the 10-13 dividing line answers WHERE geometry lives, so what stays open is how much of the consequence layer reflow2 holds, and whether @ajs wants to reopen the line for (d). Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
